Notable bugs / smells I spotted
Severity	Issue	Where
🟡 medium	In-memory rate limit — fine for Vercel single instance, breaks if multi-region. Should be Upstash/Redis.	middleware.ts:5-20
🟡 medium	Supabase service role key used in api/cases — bypasses RLS. Trust boundary is the input validation only.	app/api/cases/route.ts:58-77
🟡 medium	Hardcoded OWNER_EMAIL in admin page (sofiajuredare@gmail.com) — should be env var.	app/admin/page.tsx:8
🟡 medium	No RLS visible in any schema file — clients connect with anon key and query directly. RLS appears to be absent.	supabase/schema_v*.sql
🟡 medium	Moderator 3-approval race — votos.some(...) and votos.filter(...).length >= 3 are read after a write without a transaction. Two mods voting "approve" simultaneously could both pass the threshold check and update twice.	app/admin/page.tsx:121-128
🟡 medium	No authorization in deleteCase / openEdit — relies entirely on the client-side isOwner check. Any logged-in user with the table name can delete() directly.	app/admin/page.tsx:140-191
🟢 low	3 demo cases hardcoded in app/page.tsx — fine as fallback but should be in lib/.	app/page.tsx:15-67
🟢 low	@googlemaps/js-api-loader and cloudinary deps are installed but unused — dead weight.	package.json
🟢 low	6 separate schema_v*.sql files — should be a single ordered migration set (Supabase has supabase/migrations/ for this).	supabase/
🟢 low	react-leaflet@5.0.0 with React 19 — peer-dep warning guaranteed; works because dynamic-import hides the SSR mismatch, but fragile.	package.json
🟢 low	HTML email body in api/solicitud is template-string interpolated — XSS in the recipient's inbox if any field contains HTML.	app/api/solicitud/route.ts:32-46
🟢 low	CLAUDE.md just says @AGENTS.md and AGENTS.md just contains the Next.js agent-rules block — no real project context.	AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md

🔍 Cuidado Amiga — Full Project Audit Scope: Ai-Whisperers/cuidadoamiga-fork (29 commits, ~3.4k LoC source, 168KB repo) — a Next.js 16 + Supabase platform for documenting gender-violence cases across LATAM, with a 3-moderator approval workflow. Live at cuidadoamiga.com. This is a dual-perspective audit: engineering/architecture, and product/UX/visual. Then the engineering backlog, the CI/CD + testing plan, the public-data ingestion plan, the feature roadmap, and the abstractions/refactors. PART 1 — VISUAL & UX CRITIQUE (what the user actually sees) I didn't get a real visual capture (the web_extract tool is broken on this box) so this is from reading the rendered HTML, CSS, and component code. The site has a clear visual identity, but it's also a mixed-tone site that needs a real design pass. 1.1 The two-theme problem (🔴 critical visual bug) The site switches between two visual systems between pages with no clear reason: Page Background Border Text Vibe / (home) #f8f9fa (white-gray) #e2e8f0 #1a202c Light, clean, Maps-like /cases/new #f8fafc (slate-50) #e2e8f0 #1a202c Light /cases/[id] #f8f9fa #e2e8f0 #1a202c Light /recursos #0d0d12 (near-black) #2a2a3a #f0eaf5 Dark, activist /como-funciona #0d0d12 #2a2a3a #f0eaf5 Dark /protocolo #0d0d12 #2a2a3a #f0eaf5 Dark /unirse #0d0d12 #2a2a3a #f0eaf5 Dark /admin/login #0d0d12 #2a2a3a #f0eaf5 Dark /admin #0d0d12 #2a2a3a #f0eaf5 Dark Footer (on /) #0d0d12 #1a1a24 #9d8fad Dark sneaks under light page FAQ (on /) #0d0d12 #1a1a24 #f0eaf5 Dark sneaks under light page Result: when you scroll the homepage past the map, you go from a clean light map UI to a pitch-black FAQ section, then a pitch-black footer. The transition is jarring and looks like a render error. Fix: either commit to dark mode everywhere, light mode everywhere, or implement a real theme toggle and respect it consistently. The globals.css defines --bg-primary: #f8f9fa (light) and every "dark" page bypasses those variables with hardcoded #0d0d12. The light theme is the "real" theme per the variables; the dark sections are visual debt. 1.2 Color system is hardcoded everywhere (🟡 maintainability/brand risk) I counted 80+ hardcoded color hex literals in the JSX (not in CSS variables, not in Tailwind classes, but inline style={{ color: '#be123c' }}). Examples: Code · tsx // Repeated in MapView.tsx, CaseCard.tsx, cases/[id]/page.tsx, Filters.tsx, etc. background: '#1a1a24' border: '1px solid #2a2a3a' color: '#f0eaf5' background: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #be123c, #ec4899)' The globals.css defines only 7 CSS variables (--bg-primary, --pink, --violet, --rose). The dark theme isn't even a theme — it's just inline hex everywhere. Fix: extract a tailwind.config.ts with semantic tokens (bg-surface, text-primary, border-subtle, accent-rose) and a dark variant. 1.3 The gradient text is used 8+ times in 5 different gradients (🟡 brand inconsistency) I found these gradient-text variants: linear-gradient(135deg, #be123c, #9333ea) (footer logo) linear-gradient(135deg, #f472b6, #a855f7) (login, recursos, como-funciona, protocolo, unirse, FAQ) linear-gradient(135deg, #be123c, #ec4899) (CTAs, login button) linear-gradient(135deg, #f472b6, #a855f7) (recursos h1) linear-gradient(135deg, #f472b6, #a855f7) (duplicate in same file) Two brand gradients is fine. Five is noise. Pick one for brand display, one for CTA buttons, document them. 1.4 Visual hierarchy issues on the home page Looking at the structure: Code Navbar (light, sticky) → "Mostrando datos de demo" (yellow banner — only in demo) → Map (4:5 mobile, split-pane desktop) → Sidebar with filters + case list (desktop only) → FAQ section (suddenly DARK, no visual break) → Footer (dark) Problems: No hero section. The home page jumps straight into the map. There's no H1 explaining what Cuidado Amiga is, no mission statement, no CTA above the fold. For an advocacy site this is a huge missed conversion opportunity — first-time visitors have no context. The map is the hero, but it's not labeled as such. A first-time visitor might not realize they can click pins, filter, or that cases are moderator-verified. Need an "intro overlay" or a small explainer strip above the map. The case list is hidden by default on mobile (only shows after search), but on desktop it's the secondary panel. The mental model: "I want to see a list of cases" requires the user to know to filter first. The demo banner is too quiet — pale yellow text on a pale yellow background will be missed by 80% of visitors. If the data is demo, that should be impossible to miss. 1.5 Mobile map UX (🟡 needs work) The 4:5 aspect ratio on mobile is a nice design choice (a tall map, half the screen), but: The case list is hidden until the user clicks "Buscar". On mobile, the user can't see the data — just pins. For a documentation site, that's backwards. The data IS the product. No pin clustering: with 100+ cases the map will be unreadable. The Leaflet markercluster plugin is missing. No list alternative on mobile: there's no "view as list" toggle. A user on a slow connection or with a small phone has no way to browse cases without clicking pins one at a time. 1.6 Accessibility (🔴) I see zero accessibility features beyond aria-label on the hamburger button: Issue Where Severity without alt for case photos (relies on alt={c.nombre} which is the aggressor's name — but if the photo fails to load, no fallback) CaseCard.tsx:19 🟡 Filter buttons have no aria-pressed Filters.tsx:51 🟡 Modal in admin has no role="dialog", no focus trap, no aria-modal admin/page.tsx:297 🔴 Map popups are not screen-reader friendly — Leaflet doesn't expose marker content to AT by default MapView.tsx:85 🟡 Hamburger menu doesn't trap focus when open, doesn't close on Escape Navbar.tsx:71 🟡 Color contrast: --text-secondary: #64748b on #f8f9fa is 4.4:1 (AA borderline) and #9d8fad on #0d0d12 is 3.7:1 (fails AA for body text) globals.css + inline 🔴 Form fields have no
